title: The Paramount record and the So Different Four lineup
summary: Allen and Jones go over the Paramount record of Homeward Bound Blues and Tiger Rag, its date and sidemen (Tapley, the Turners). Jones's nose whistle is played for the tape.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: The Homer Bond.
Homer Bond and Tiger Rag.
If you have Tiger Rag on, it should be easy to find because people bought Tiger Rag.
Tiger Rag on the one side and the Homer Bond on the other.
Yeah, and this is Paramount and then what year?
I think it's around 22, I'd say 22 or 23.

Well, it was very early in the first period of Paramount. Inc. must have started with them right at the outset, didn't it? They had ink started with them just as soon as they started recording stuff on the south side. Yeah, yeah. Inc. must have been there very early. Well, I'll see what I can find. He stayed on the south side, right at 28th and LaSalle at the time.
Did these fellas all come from Louisville with you?
No, no, neither. He lived with his father.
You don't know where Tapley came from originally?
No, I do not.
James Turner?
He lived here already. He was an original Louisville Jug Band. Mm-hmm. That, they're the names you don't can't remember the banjo. Mm-hmm.

Well, this is the group that made the Paramount, anyway, and you used a nose whistle on that. Yeah. And it was called Jones So Different Four. So Different Four. No, I never made but one record.
This is your record, okay.
It's the most record I ever made. Uh-huh.

Do you ever hear a nose whistle? No. Play it for him a little bit, and we'll see how it records, and then I'll play it back on then. Gee, I appreciate that.
